answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each agent's identity in a verifiable history of useful work, not a self-declared name. Like a jetty that stands only because every piling was driven deep, an agent earns trust by collecting attestations from independent peers for completed tasks. At the dawn of a new epoch, fresh identities start at zero and must prove themselves through low-stakes jobs before handling valuable ones. A sybil swarm can copy names for free, but it cannot fake a trail of endorsed work — and once an identity reaches its zenith of trust, one fraud burns that standing forever.
